Context: the page is an 'Additamentum ad § 40', a supplement to Jacobi's Fundamenta Nova §40. That section gives product and Lambert-series expansions for k, k', K, kK and k'K in terms of the nome q. Riemann announces his aim. Jacobi's formulas become interesting when |q| = 1, because they then yield functions of one variable that are discontinuous at every value of the argument. Most of the series diverge on |q| = 1, so he first integrates the formulas 1-7 term by term against dq/q, starting from q = 0. This produces series that can converge there. Modern dictionary: k = θ2²/θ3², k' = θ4²/θ3², 2K/π = θ3², 2kK/π = θ2², 2k'K/π = θ4² (nome q). Throughout, F(q) = ∫_0^q f(q) dq/q means F has q·F'(q) = f and F(0) = 0.

(48) Jacobi: k = 4√q ∏_{n≥1} ((1+q^{2n})/(1+q^{2n-1}))^4. Hence log k − log 4√q = 4Σ_n [log(1+q^{2n}) − log(1+q^{2n-1})] = 4Σ_{n,m≥1} (−1)^{n+m+1} q^{nm}/n [my step: expand each log and regroup]. Integrating gives ∫_0 (log k − log 4√q) dq/q = 4Σ_{n≥1} (−1)^n log(1+q^n)/n² = −4log(1+q) + (4/4)log(1+q²) − (4/9)log(1+q³) + (4/16)log(1+q⁴) − … A first attempt with an extra dq/q inside the parentheses is struck.

(49) k' = ∏ ((1−q^{2n−1})/(1+q^{2n−1}))^4. So −log k' = 8Σ_{n,m odd} q^{nm}/m, which is symmetric in n and m. Integrating: ∫_0 −log k' dq/q = 4Σ_{n odd} (1/n²) log((1+q^n)/(1−q^n)).

(50) 2K/π = θ3² = ∏ (1−q^{2n})²(1+q^{2n−1})^4. Its logarithm equals 4Σ_{n odd} Σ_m (−1)^{m+1} q^{nm}/n [my identification; checked through q⁴]. Hence ∫_0 log(2K/π) dq/q = 4Σ_{n odd} log(1+q^n)/n² = 4log(1+q) + (4/9)log(1+q³) + (4/25)log(1+q⁵) + …

(51) Jacobi's Lambert series: 2K/π − 1 = 4Σ_n q^n/(1+q^{2n}) = 4Σ_{n≥1} Σ_{m≥0} (−1)^m q^{n(2m+1)}. Integrating gives 4Σ_{n,m} (−1)^m q^{n(2m+1)}/(n(2m+1)), which Riemann sums two ways.
- Over n first: −4Σ_m (−1)^m log(1−q^{2m+1})/(2m+1) = −4log(1−q) + (4/3)log(1−q³) − (4/5)log(1−q⁵) + … An initial '4log(1+q)' is struck.
- Over m first: 4Σ_n arctan(q^n)/n. With arctan x = (i/2)log((1−ix)/(1+ix)) this is Σ_n (2i/n) log((1−q^n i)/(1+q^n i)).

(52) 2kK/π = θ2² = 4Σ_{n odd} q^{n/2}/(1+q^n) = 4Σ_{n odd} Σ_m (−1)^m q^{n(2m+1)/2}. Integrating gives 8Σ (−1)^m q^{n(2m+1)/2}/(n(2m+1)).
- Summing over odd n with Σ_{n odd} x^n/n = ½log((1+x)/(1−x)): 4Σ_m ((−1)^m/(2m+1)) log((1+q^{(2m+1)/2})/(1−q^{(2m+1)/2})) = 4log((1+√q)/(1−√q)) − (4/3)log((1+√q³)/(1−√q³)) + (4/5)log(…) …
- Summing over m: 8Σ_{n odd} arctan(q^{n/2})/n = 4iΣ_{n odd} (1/n) log((1−i√qⁿ)/(1+i√qⁿ)).
The line '4i log((1−√q i)/(1+√q i)) + (4i/3) log(…) + (4i/5) log(…)' sits physically after '53) … =' because of lack of space. Its content, all signs + and half-integer powers, is exactly this second form of (52), not of (53).

(53) 2k'K/π − 1 = θ4² − 1 = 4Σ_n (−1)^n q^n/(1+q^{2n}). Integrating gives 4Σ_n Σ_m (−1)^{n+m} q^{n(2m+1)}/(n(2m+1)).
- Summed over n: −4Σ_m ((−1)^m/(2m+1)) log(1+q^{2m+1}) = −(4/1)log(1+q) + (4/3)log(1+q³) − (4/5)log(1+q⁵) + … The exponents are visibly overwritten in the MS.
- Summed over m: 4Σ_n (−1)^n arctan(q^n)/n = −2i log((1−qi)/(1+qi)) + (2i/2)log((1−q²i)/(1+q²i)) − (2i/3)log((1−q³i)/(1+q³i)) + … Denominators and exponents are overwritten in the MS.

Purpose: these integrated (dilogarithm-type / arctan-Lambert) series converge, or at least behave better, on |q| = 1. Riemann then (next page) re-expands them as power series with Jacobi's notation and states a general Abelian-type limit theorem. This is the preparation for studying the boundary behaviour of the modular functions as q → e^{2πi·rational}.
errors: Struck false start in (48): 'log k dq/q' inside the parentheses; the final intended formula is ∫_0 (log k − log 4√q) dq/q.
Struck false start in (51): '4 log(1+q)' before '−4 log(1−q)'.

In (53) several exponents/denominators are overwritten (e.g. q^3 over another digit, a denominator corrected to 3/5). The intended and correct final form is −4log(1+q) + (4/3)log(1+q³) − (4/5)log(1+q⁵) …, and −2i Σ (−1)^{n+1} (1/n) log((1−qⁿi)/(1+qⁿi)).
Placement slip: the line '4i log((1−√q i)/(1+√q i)) + …' written after '53) =' is mathematically the second expression for (52); as an expression for (53) it would be false.
Otherwise all formulas checked (coefficients verified by hand to low order) are correct; term-by-term rearrangements of double series are justified for |q| < 1 by absolute convergence (implicit).

results.what: Integrated log-expansions of k, k', 2K/π: ∫_0 (log k − log4√q) dq/q = 4Σ(−1)^n log(1+qⁿ)/n², ∫_0 −log k' dq/q = 4Σ_{n odd} log((1+qⁿ)/(1−qⁿ))/n², ∫_0 log(2K/π) dq/q = 4Σ_{n odd} log(1+qⁿ)/n²
results.modern_name: Termwise integration of Jacobi's product formulas; Eichler-type integrals / dilogarithmic q-series of theta quotients
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (fragment published by Dedekind, Werke 1876); underlying expansions Jacobi 1829

results.what: Double-summation identities for integrated Lambert series of θ3², θ2², θ4² as sums of log((1±qᵏ)/(1∓qᵏ)) and of arctan(qⁿ)/n written via complex logarithms
results.modern_name: Lambert series of sums of two squares (r2(n)) integrated; arctan Lambert series
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (Lambert series for 2K/π etc.); this integrated form Riemann, published in 'Fragmente über die Grenzfälle der elliptischen Modulfunctionen'

results.what: Program: use these integrated series to study the limit |q| → 1 and obtain functions discontinuous at every (rational) point
results.modern_name: Boundary behaviour of modular forms / Riemann's study of limiting cases; precursor of Dedekind eta transformation and Dedekind sums (Dedekind's commentary)

deep.surprise_reason: This page is the opening of Riemann's known fragment on the limiting cases of the elliptic modular functions. Dedekind published it in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876, Nachlass XXVIII) with a famous commentary. The formulas are correct, routine consequences of Jacobi's §40 expansions and are already attributed to Riemann.
